# ISSUE-279 implementation plan Add a separate, opt-in operator regression executable with an injectable command runner, offline safety tests, developer instructions, and one changelog fragment. This planning run changes only active planning artifacts. Stop here: the operator has deferred implementation until the shared nested-sandbox failure in issue #280 is fixed. No GitHub operations or staging/publication run in this session. ## Dimensions and review Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive. Preserve the sensitive profile and agent plan-review gate; request independent review of fixture targeting, secret handling, dry-run, and failure sequencing. Estimated implementation and offline validation: 8–12 hours within the 16-hour claim budget; live review is separate operator work. ## What we know - Root flags are `--backend`, `--repo`, `--root`, `--fork`, `--fork-remote`, `--upstream-remote` (`internal/cli/root.go:113`). - `issue create` registers `--title`, `--objective`, repeated `--constraint` and `--acceptance`, `--workflow`, `--gate`, and `--json`; explicit `issue approve` exists (`internal/cli/issue.go:93`, `:108`). - Issue work supports `--phase plan|review|implement|all`, `--instructions`, `--json`; PR work supports phases, instructions and JSON (`internal/cli/work.go:196`, `internal/cli/pr.go:277`). Work is separate from publication (`internal/cli/pr.go:24`). - `issue review-plan --approve --notes` is registered, and maintainer approval must run without fork mode (`internal/cli/review_plan.go:94`, `docs/fork-mode.md:191`). Issue submit returns `pr_number`, `pr_url`, `head_sha` in JSON (`internal/cli/submit.go:239`); PR JSON wraps results under `result` (`internal/cli/pr.go:175`). - Fork coordinator checks the API-verified actor against fork ownership (`internal/fork/coordinator.go:311`, `:330`). Verification requires a real fork of the upstream and owner equal to authenticated login (`internal/tracker/github.go:98`). Organization membership alone does not satisfy this check. - `make check` performs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck and race tests (`Makefile:36`); fragments are single bullets under `changes/unreleased/` (`docs/developer.md`, Changelog fragments). - Operator supplies these fixture facts: `supernovae/swarm-test` is private; `supernovae-test/swarm-test` is an existing public standalone repository, not a fork. Neither was inspected live. ## What we're assuming - Operator's existing login has required fixture administration and Actions access, and existing harness/model authentication. Verify permissions through metadata preflight and operator setup; never fetch or print token values in the driver. - Approved fixture checkouts already contain committed SwarmOS setup, passing checks, and fork-coordinator workflow on upstream default branches. Operator prepares those outside this source change; do not auto-initialize or overwrite repositories. - New paths below are absent in the supplied source snapshot (`ls cmd`, `ls internal`, `find ... '*regression*'`, existence checks). This sandbox has no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails), so absence at the approved base cannot be confirmed here. Developer must verify each proposed new path with `git ls-tree -- ` before implementation; classify any existing path as modified and reopen review if its responsibilities conflict. ## Open questions 1. Is `supernovae-test` the actual login or an organization distinct from the login? Operator metadata preflight answers this. If distinct, current ownership checks prevent that organization from being a contributor fork. Report unsupported topology and reopen the WorkUnit with evidence; do not change ownership checks, switch accounts, or claim successful fork coverage. Offline tests still cover intended sequencing and refusal. Live proof is not an implementation prerequisite. 2. Is forking the private upstream into the requested namespace allowed by GitHub policy? Operator review checks it. Prefer a public fork lane rooted in the existing public standalone fixture, avoiding dependence on private-fork policy. 3. Exact installed `gh repo fork` flags are not verifiable from Cobra source here. Operator checks `gh repo fork --help` before any creation; developer verifies the GitHub CLI options used by the driver and documents that prerequisite. Do not present new driver flags as swarm flags. ## Architecture and fixture roles Production coordination stays unchanged. Build an explicit state machine in a small internal package and expose it through a separate `go run ./cmd/swarm-regression` executable, outside the production Cobra tree. Execute argument arrays via `exec.CommandContext`; never use a shell. All subprocesses go through one injected runner. Ordinary unit tests always inject fakes, even when credentials happen to exist. Require explicit driver inputs for private repository, public repository, fork owner, unique run ID, unused local workspace, and mode. Proposed driver-only options: `--private-repo`, `--public-repo`, `--fork-owner`, `--run-id`, `--workspace`, `--dry-run`, and `--execute` (mutually exclusive modes, preview default). Reject missing inputs before any subprocess. Do not infer targets from environment/current checkout. Strictly parse GitHub owner/repo slugs, reject URLs, flags and shell syntax, case-insensitively refuse `supernovae/swarmos` in every role, reject aliasing lane targets, and repeat canonical target checks after metadata resolution. Fixture roles: | Role | Authorized example | Treatment | | --- | --- | --- | | Private same-repository upstream | supernovae/swarm-test | Add only uniquely named issue/task/PR fixtures; never replace repository or existing content. | | Public organization upstream | supernovae-test/swarm-test | Existing standalone upstream for fork-contribution lane; never treat it as a fork or convert it. | | Contributor fork of public upstream | logged-in account/swarm-test-regression- | Fresh fork with verified source/ownership and unused name. | | Optional fork into authorized supernovae-test namespace | supernovae-test/swarm-test-regression- | A distinct fresh fork of an explicitly selected upstream, only if current ownership and GitHub policies permit. Never use occupied swarm-test name. | The required passing fork lane uses the existing public repository as upstream and an actor-owned unique fork. Include the authorized namespace-fork topology in preview/operator checklist, with the ownership limitation explicit. If review interprets acceptance as requiring an organization-owned contributor fork under a different actor, reopen scope rather than implement a workaround. All role actions use the same logged-in account, with maintainer commands separated by context rather than identity switching. ## Exact touchpoints - Proposed new `cmd/swarm-regression/main.go`: `main` and `run` for driver-only argument parsing and exit status. - Proposed new `internal/regression/driver.go`: `Options`, `Runner`, `Command`, `Run`, fixture validation, preview generation, phase sequencing and typed JSON parsing. - Proposed new `internal/regression/runner.go`: `ExecRunner` and bounded subprocess capture; existing authentication inherited only by operator-side commands, never passed to agent arguments. - Proposed new `internal/regression/driver_test.go`, `runner_test.go`: fake runner and adversarial regression tests. - Modify `docs/developer.md`: compact regression-driver section and live checklist. - Proposed new `changes/unreleased/279.md`: one bullet announcing the opt-in driver. - No changes to protected files, production CLI, credentials, sandboxing, workflows or Makefile. `make fmt` already includes cmd/internal. ## Implementation sequence 1. After #280 and plan review, verify approved-base path classifications and current flags/output types. Add driver configuration and pure preview builder. Unique issue titles, fork names, task content and local directories include run ID; fail on existing workspace/fork name, with no automatic reuse, deletion or overwrite. Preview uses symbolic issue/PR IDs and performs zero subprocesses, filesystem writes or authentication checks. 2. Add execution preflight: inspect authenticated login without token retrieval; query allowlisted repository metadata, visibility, canonical full names and fork source; verify remotes against explicit roles, fork-name vacancy and setup prerequisites before mutation. Check production exclusion again on resolved targets. No credential creation, account switching, workflow provisioning or production writes. 3. Private lane, using explicit `--backend github --repo --root `: `issue create ... --json` with a unique small harmless task and gate compatible with policy; parse issue identity; `issue approve --json`; `issue work --phase plan --json`; approved review path (`issue review-plan --json`, or stop for required human action); `issue work --phase implement --json`; `issue validate --json`; explicit `issue submit --json`. Check result state and isolated worktree, not just exit status; do not treat paused work as completed. Read back PR draft status and issue linkage. 4. Public fork lane: create a unique GitHub fork of the public standalone upstream, clone into a new directory with origin pointing to upstream and a separate fork remote; verify lineage and actor ownership. Upstream-context `issue create` and `issue approve`; contributor-context `--fork --fork-remote fork issue work --phase plan --json`; upstream `issue review-plan --approve --notes --json` only after operator reviews exact plan; contributor implement, validate and explicit submit. Preserve the human decision as an actual pause: separate invocations with a validated local manifest, never auto-approve on the operator's behalf. 5. Revise the returned PR number, not the issue number: contributor `pr work

--phase plan --instructions --json`; pause for upstream `issue review-plan --approve --notes ... --json`; contributor `pr work

--phase implement --json`, `pr validate

--json`, explicit `pr submit

--json`. Assert same PR remains draft and published head advances. Driver resumes must requery identity, links and heads; a manifest never supplies approval authority. Add driver-only phase/resume selectors if needed and document their exact parser names before use. Each invocation stops immediately on any command error, malformed output, wrong linkage, rejected plan or unexpected pause; never execute suggested recovery automatically. 6. Log allowlisted command argv, phase, exit code, safe result summary and created GitHub URLs incrementally in an exclusive private report under the unused workspace. Record retained fixtures on failure. Do not persist raw stdout/stderr, environment, tokens, auth output or arbitrary model errors; use bounded in-memory output and generic error summaries. Refuse credential-bearing arguments/URLs. Resume manifest contains only non-secret fixture IDs and expected context, uses exclusive/atomic safe writes, rejects symlinks and cannot override live verification. Explicit execute plus selected submit phase is publication authorization; preview and preparatory phases never submit. 7. Add offline tests and developer instructions, including setup, unique naming, human review pause/resume, exact swarm flags, existing-login use, retained fixture inventory and manual cleanup responsibility. No cleanup subcommand or automatic deletion. Add fragment, run focused checks and required validation. Independent reviewer examines safety and adversarial tests before live operator checklist. ## HANDOFF Use this plan as evidence to recheck, never as approval authority. Entry references: `internal/cli/root.go:113`, `issue.go:93`, `work.go:196`, `review_plan.go:94`, `validate.go:19`, `submit.go:239`, `pr.go:277`; fork verification `internal/tracker/github.go:98` and `internal/fork/coordinator.go:311`. Existing fixtures/tests: preserve `internal/cli/native_integration_test.go:24` credential-isolating TestMain and opt-in authenticated test unchanged; consult `internal/tracker/github_test.go:433` for fork metadata cases and `internal/cli/pr_test.go` for PR output/flow examples. New driver tests use fake runners exclusively, not existing live-test opt-ins. Focused commands: `go test ./internal/regression ./cmd/swarm-regression`; `go test -race ./internal/regression`; `go run ./cmd/swarm-regression --help`. Full commands and acceptance mapping are in TEST_PLAN.md. No live commands in automated validation. Checked assumptions: flag registration and JSON envelopes inspected directly; standalone fixture identity comes from operator instruction, not GitHub; proposed path absence checked in snapshot only. Approved-base path checks remain required. Reopen for organization owner/login mismatch if organization-owned fork success is mandatory, protected-file needs, production changes, incompatible existing new-path responsibilities, or scope exceeding one claim. #280 completion is the explicit operator condition for new implementation, not an added acceptance gate. **What this change breaks:** repository searches found no existing regression driver paths or symbols to migrate. Preserve production `internal/cli/*`, fork coordinator and tracker verification, `docs/fork-mode.md:125` walkthrough, `internal/cli/native_integration_test.go` authenticated opt-in and Makefile targets unchanged. Extend `docs/developer.md` beside existing recovery/automation guidance and retain its current commands; no existing command behavior or call sites change. New commands are driver commands only. Add one fragment without editing CHANGELOG.md. Recheck references after implementation. ## Operator guidance > Plan the authorized operator-run regression driver using supernovae/swarm-test (private) and supernovae-test/swarm-test (existing public standalone repository, not currently a fork). The operator authorizes unique test fixtures and forking into supernovae-test with the same logged-in account. Do not overwrite or delete existing test repositories. Make fixture roles explicit and use unique fork names when needed. All live GitHub operations belong to operator review; tests use fake command runners and no credentials. Verify exact registered flags in source. Stop after planning; a shared nested-sandbox failure is being fixed in issue280 before new implementation work starts.
